title: Woe to the whitewashed tombs
english: "Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like whitewashed tombs, which look beautiful on the outside but inside are full of the bones of the dead. So you also look righteous on the outside, but inside you are full of hypocrisy and lawlessness" (Matthew 23:27-28). Every pretended righteousness is a dead righteousness.
translator_notes: Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Origen is commenting on Jesus' woe against the scribes and Pharisees, quoting Matthew 23:27-28 and then adding his own moral gloss.

title: The Scribes' Burden, Yoke, and Shut Kingdom
english: Those who sit on Moses' seat do all their works to be seen by others (Matthew 23:2-3, 5). The bodily burden of the law is heavy; the yoke of Christ is sweet and the burden light (Matthew 11:30) — the Gospel is a spiritual law. They shut the kingdom of heaven, neither entering themselves nor allowing others to enter (Matthew 23:13). Glory to Christ. Amen.
orientation: Origen is commenting on Jesus' woes against the scribes and Pharisees, just after explaining that all pretended righteousness is dead.
